scores.success_why: [E] One video, no first-hand claim, and the $50k claim is excluded; UK drone rules, equipment and field work make a £300, 5-hour test implausible.
scores.agent_why: [E] Agents could handle booking and records, but recovery and spraying require a qualified operator and drone in the field.
scores.fit_why: [E] Selling to agricultural operators locally breaks the local-business constraint; physical work also conflicts with the hours and budget.
scores.automation_why: [E] Some admin can be automated, but acquisition and nearly all delivery are physical.
scores.staleness_note: Single 2026 video; recheck UK drone permissions, agricultural spraying requirements, equipment costs and local demand.
scores.one_line: Field service with weak evidence and poor fit for Ricardo's constraints.

scores.success_why: [E] A single 2025 video gives no outcome evidence; production, installation and maintenance need equipment, customers and time beyond the test budget.
scores.agent_why: [E] Agents can assist with designs and quotes, but prospecting, fabrication, installation and maintenance need people on site.
scores.fit_why: [E] The described customers are businesses, and on-site work conflicts with the local-sales constraint and limited hours.
scores.automation_why: [E] Design and scheduling can be partly automated; sales, physical production and installation cannot.
scores.staleness_note: Single 2025 video; recheck UK demand, production and installation costs, and any site-specific requirements.
scores.one_line: A capital- and labour-heavy local trade, with no evidence of a low-cost entry point.

scores.success_why: [E] First-hand figures show scale at an existing laundromat, not a solo startup; premises, equipment, transport and local commercial accounts exceed the budget and time available.
scores.agent_why: [E] Agents can manage bookings and billing, but washing, folding, stain treatment and transport are physical operations.
scores.fit_why: [E] Selling to local commercial accounts breaks the hard constraint; the operating model also requires substantial capital and labour.
scores.automation_why: [E] Admin is automatable, but most delivery and quality control are physical.
scores.staleness_note: The 2026 first-hand claims describe one US location; recheck UK utilities, equipment and vehicle costs, contract rates and demand.
scores.one_line: Evidence of an established operation's volume, not a viable part-time test for Ricardo.

scores.success_why: [E] Response and cost claims are unverified; each campaign needs local business customers and repeated physical delivery, with no stated pricing.
scores.agent_why: [E] Agents can target routes and produce flyers, but finding clients, assembling packages and distributing them are manual.
scores.fit_why: [E] It sells marketing to local businesses and requires physical distribution, breaking the local-sales constraint and exceeding the time budget.
scores.automation_why: [E] Targeting, copy and reporting can be automated; sales and delivery dominate the work.
scores.staleness_note: Single 2025 anecdote; recheck UK customer demand, campaign economics and rules affecting flyer distribution and access.
scores.one_line: Low-cost materials do not solve the local sales and manual-delivery bottlenecks.

scores.success_why: [E] The only evidence is a hypothetical example with no fee model; outcomes depend on winning local partners and their customers' response.
scores.agent_why: [E] Agents can identify prospects and track referrals, but partner trust, negotiation and campaign oversight need human involvement.
scores.fit_why: [E] It requires selling to local businesses and, as described, partner marketing to individuals through text/email without stated consent; both conflict with Ricardo's constraints.
scores.automation_why: [E] Prospect research and tracking can be automated, but partnership acquisition and compliant campaign approval need human work.
scores.uk_legal_reason: The proposed partner promotion uses texts and email to customer lists. UK marketing texts to individuals generally need consent, and the dossier gives no evidence of consent for third-party offers.
scores.staleness_note: Single 2025 hypothetical; recheck partner demand and current PECR requirements, including consent for third-party customer-list promotions.
scores.one_line: The referral concept has no clear revenue model and its proposed outreach is not established as PECR-compliant.

scores.success_why: [E] Standardising a service could support recurring fees, but the single video names no niche, proven demand or first-hand results; AI also makes generic services easier to copy.
scores.agent_why: [E] Agents can handle research, intake, routine delivery and billing for a tightly scoped service, while acquisition, quality control and exceptions need Ricardo.
scores.fit_why: [E] A remote technical service for limited companies could fit his skills and constraints, though the dossier does not establish which service he would enjoy or sell.
scores.automation_why: [E] Routine production and admin can be automated, but finding and retaining clients and reviewing work remain significant.
scores.staleness_note: Single 2025 general discussion; validate a specific UK niche, willingness to pay and competition before relying on the model.
scores.one_line: Most adaptable cluster, but success depends on choosing a narrow, defensible service.

scores.success_why: [E] A single video and non-first-hand price claim do not establish current demand; design subscriptions face heavy competition and AI commoditisation.
scores.agent_why: [E] Agents can manage briefs, drafts and billing, but taste, revisions and client communication still need close human review.
scores.fit_why: [E] It can be remote and avoid personal branding, but design is not an evident technical fit and ongoing client work strains the time limit.
scores.automation_why: [E] Drafting and administration can be automated, while art direction, revisions, sales and support still take time.
scores.staleness_note: Single 2025 video cites Design Pickle and a $1,500/month price; recheck current competitor offers, pricing and buyer demand.
scores.one_line: Recurring revenue is possible, but the design-heavy delivery is a weak skills and time match.

scores.success_why: [E] The event is only a proposal from one 2025 video; UK tax work requires market-specific knowledge, and seasonal client delivery is hard to fit into five hours weekly.
scores.agent_why: [E] Agents can help collect documents and prepare drafts, but tax review, client questions and filing responsibility need expert oversight.
scores.fit_why: [E] The proposed event and explanatory content rely on a visible expert presence; that conflicts with the face/brand constraint and adds in-person work.
scores.automation_why: [E] Intake and document extraction can be automated, but sales, exception handling and accurate review remain substantial.
scores.staleness_note: Single 2025 proposal appears US-oriented; recheck UK tax-agent requirements, current tax-year workflows and event economics.
scores.one_line: The proposed event-led acquisition is a poor match for Ricardo's time and no-personal-brand constraints.
